experiments.title: Self-teaching encoder-generator (JEPA encoder teaches G)
experiments.question: Can an encoder trained only on view alignment + a regularizer teach a generator through its own judgment, without pixel loss, and does the generator exploit the judge? Arms: direct z Wasserstein vs LeJEPA projector + SIGReg. Notes: imagenet-selfteach/jepagen/README.md
experiments.verdict: No arm teaches a generator. All three G exploit the judge: own-judge 0.06-0.11, baseline-AE judge 0.92-1.09 (1 = random image). Previews: periodic textures with each image's palette and a faint layout. Encoders did not collapse (z_rank 10.6-18.5). Best on the outside judge: wassproj 0.92, sigreg 0.93, wass 1.09.

experiments.title: Projector-free Wasserstein vs LeJEPA (Imagenette)
experiments.question: Can the tuned 4-term Wasserstein regularizer train useful ViT-S/8 features with no projector (B), matching LeJEPA with its MLP+BN projector (A)? C = SIGReg with no projector. Score: frozen linear probe on native 384-d features, official val, 3 paired seeds.
experiments.falsifier: B below A by more than the seed spread (mean ± sd over 3 paired seeds) at the final step

experiments.title: AE regularizer strength and power (p 1 vs 2)
experiments.question: Does the Gaussian (Wasserstein) regularizer disrupt self-teaching AE convergence through latent churn, and does squaring it, λ r_ref/p (r/r_ref)^p with p 2, widen the usable λ range? Write-up: /regx-power.html

pages.title: Write-up: past the noise floor a stronger regularizer adds only churn; p = 2 does not widen the range

runs.label: p1 λ0 s44 5k, continued from p1-lam0.5-s44:20000
p1 λ0.5 s44 40k, continued from p1-lam0.5-s44:20000
p1 λ0.05 s44 40k, continued from ref-s44:20000
p1 λ1.58 s44 20k, debiased (4/n removed per term)
p1 λ15.8 s44 20k, debiased (4/n removed per term)
p1 λ15.8 s45 20k, debiased (4/n removed per term)
p1 λ0.05 s44 40k, debiased (4/n removed per term), continued from ref-s44:20000
p1 λ0.5 s44 60k, debiased (4/n removed per term)
p1 λ0.05 s44 60k, debiased (4/n removed per term)
p1 λ0.05 s44 20k, latent noise scaled to std(z)
p1 λ0.05 s44 40k, latent noise scaled to std(z), continued from ref-s44:20000
p1 λ0.05 s44 40k, debiased (4/n removed per term), latent noise scaled to std(z), continued from ref-s44:20000

experiments.verdict: Keep plain λ = 0.05. From λ 0.5 up, r sits on its batch noise floor 2(4/B)^2 = 0.0078 and more strength only adds churn. p = 2 gives no gain. Debiasing (4/n removed per term) halves the damage at λ 15.8 on 2 seeds, but gives no gain at λ 0.05 (60k: 0.0042 against 0.0041). At 60k, λ 0.05 (0.0041) beats λ 0.5 (0.0083).

experiments.title: Freeze ablation after a 64 to 128 px scale-up
experiments.question: Which modules must re-learn after a scale-up, and does freezing the rest save wall-clock time?
experiments.verdict: Freezing saves only 15-50% step time and costs more steps than it saves.

experiments.title: AE resolution scaling (Spark)
experiments.question: What is the fastest wall-clock route to a high-resolution AE by training at lower resolution first, and what has to re-learn after a scale-up?
experiments.verdict: 64 px at 25k scaled to 128 px reached test MSE 0.0066 2.15x faster than 128 px from scratch; late switches adapt in about 1k steps but are slower overall.

experiments.title: STL-10 25M: norm combos and robustness of L4
experiments.question: Which core in/out norm combination is needed, and how robust is the L4 setup to lr and beta2?
experiments.verdict: The per-token input norm is the necessary piece; lr 2e-4 collapses sometimes, lr 3e-4 reliably.

experiments.title: STL-10 25M: fixes for lr 3e-4 collapse
experiments.question: Which architecture change (GELU, qk-norm, token init, branch-output RMSNorm) lets the AE survive lr 3e-4?
experiments.verdict: P4 (token init 0.02 + branch-output RMSNorm with gain 1e-4) was the first setup to survive lr 3e-4.

experiments.title: STL-10 25M: failure-mode diagnosis
experiments.question: Why does the decoder collapse (ww too high, view too high, lr too high)?
experiments.verdict: Flat-SWD gradient noise drives z drift (fix: 1024 slices, E1); high view weight gives rank collapse; lr 3e-4 gives a static runaway in decoder MLPs.

experiments.title: STL-10 25M: norm placement, weights and lr (first night)
experiments.question: Which norm placement, view/regularizer weights and lr keep the 25M self-teach AE from collapsing?
experiments.verdict: Stream/stream collapses (B0); per-token in+out at 3:1 weights is healthy (M1_vw03); lr 3e-4 and beta2 0.95 break the per-token base. Eval metrics of B1-L4 are invalid (hook bug).
